title: Turn the table, lose the wobble
hook: Can a turn help this square equal-leg table?

knows: Everyday objects have sizes, positions and amounts
doesNotKnow: The illustrated signed gap crosses zero during a quarter turn. For square equal-leg tables on suitably gentle continuous ground, a balanced position exists.

misconception: The two pictured methods are interchangeable without checking their mechanism or constraints.

claims.text: Contact means the four feet touch the ground. It does not mean the tabletop is level. Equal legs and suitably gentle continuous ground belong to the stated model; unequal legs fall outside it.
claims.source: Baritompa, Löwen, Polster & Ross, Mathematical table turning revisited, full text opened 2026-10-14 at https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0511490. Square equal-leg table, continuous ground and slope/leg length conditions; proof of sign change and balanced position. Our cosine gap is an illustration, not a solution of the full contact geometry. recall.question: You turn a square equal-leg table on gentle, continuous ground until all four feet touch. What do you now know?
options: It has stopped rocking; the top may still slope
A table with one short leg would settle the same way
recall.why: Contact means the four feet touch the ground. It does not mean the tabletop is level. Equal legs and suitably gentle continuous ground belong to the stated model; unequal legs fall outside it.
